steps.title: Declare the boundary: Yield-based dependency cleanup

blocks.text: Acquire the resource before yield. The dependency supplies the yielded resource to the operation.
Surround yield with try/finally and release the resource in finally, covering successful use and exceptions.
Default request scope ends after response sending. Depends(provider, scope="function") ends after handler completion, before the response is sent.
If you catch an exception without intentionally handling it, re-raise it. Do not conceal the failure from FastAPI.

blocks.title: Resource ownership and scope boundaries

nodes.label: Default request scope: finally releases resource

blocks.alt_text: Resource ownership and scope boundaries: Acquire resource; Yield to operation; Operation uses resource; Handler completion; Declared scope; Function scope: finally releases resource; Send response; Default request scope: finally releases resource; Exceptional use; Re-raise unhandled exception; finally: release resource

blocks.text: Trace acquisition, yield and operation use separately. Put release in finally so both successful and exceptional paths clean up. Default request scope ends after response sending; function scope ends after handler completion, before sending. If a caught exception was not intentionally handled, re-raise it. Yield is not a promise that every dependency ends at handler completion.

steps.title: Check the boundary: Yield-based dependency cleanup
steps.lede: Use the supplied order-service scenario to reason about this contract.

correct.message: Finally releases on successful and exceptional exits; re-raising preserves the unhandled exception. Request scope cleans up after sending; function scope after handler completion but before sending.

incorrect.message: If you chose suppression, re-raise a caught exception you have not intentionally handled; finally still releases the resource. If you chose reversed scope timing, remember: default request cleanup follows response sending, while function cleanup follows handler completion and precedes sending.

public.prompt: Which pattern releases resources on both exits, preserves an unhandled caught exception, and correctly distinguishes cleanup scopes?

options.text: Release in finally, re-raise the unhandled exception; default request scope cleans up after response sending, while function scope cleans up after handler completion but before sending.
Release in finally, suppress the unhandled caught exception; default request scope cleans up after response sending, while function scope cleans up after handler completion but before sending.
Release in finally, re-raise the unhandled exception; default request scope cleans up before response sending, while function scope cleans up after sending.

option_1.message: Finally releases on successful and exceptional exits; re-raising preserves the unhandled exception. Request scope cleans up after sending; function scope after handler completion but before sending.

option_2.message: Suppressing the unhandled caught exception conceals it even though finally releases the resource.

option_3.message: The scope timings are reversed: default request cleanup follows response sending, while function cleanup follows handler completion and precedes sending.

public.prompt: Complete provider with try/finally around yield resource and resource.close() on exit. Do not catch and conceal exceptions. The supplied boundary harness verifies successful and exceptional exits and compares default request-scope release after response sending with function-scope release after handler completion but before sending. The pinned FastAPI lacks the scope keyword, so this comparison is an explicit supplied boundary model, not a claim that this older runtime supports Depends(provider, scope="function").

remediation_steps.title: Try the contrast: Yield-based dependency cleanup

blocks.text: Surround yield with try/finally and release the resource in finally, covering successful use and exceptions.
If you catch an exception without intentionally handling it, re-raise it. Do not conceal the failure from FastAPI.
For the supplied resource, cleanup on failure and failure visibility are separate: finally releases it, while re-raising an unhandled exception keeps the failure visible.

Default request scope releases the resource after the response is sent. With Depends(provider, scope="function"), release happens after the handler finishes and before the response is sent. Reversing these timings is incorrect even when finally releases the resource and unhandled exceptions are re-raised.
